subject: current_process
statement: Today HR collects onboarding data via a Word document and an Excel file, and then types everything into the receiving parties' portals by hand.

anchors.quote: I have a Word document, then an Excel file, and then I type everything into the portals by hand.

subject: current_process
statement: Manual onboarding is time-consuming: last month HR spent a full afternoon on two new hires.

anchors.quote: Last month I spent a full afternoon on two new hires.

subject: hiring_volume
statement: Muster AG hires around twenty people per year (more in summer) and has about 150 employees, mostly in Zurich.

anchors.quote: Around twenty. More in summer. We're about a hundred and fifty people now, mostly here in Zurich.

subject: source_tax_questionnaire
statement: Source tax is HR's biggest pain point: because HR doesn't know in advance who must answer the source tax questions, the whole questionnaire is sent to everybody, which annoys Swiss employees.

anchors.quote: So I send the whole questionnaire to everybody, and the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

subject: source_tax_questionnaire
statement: Source tax questions should be asked only to employees who are subject to source tax, not to everybody.

anchors.quote: Because I never know up front who has to answer those questions.
the Swiss people get annoyed, and they call me.

judge_note: Reasonable inference: Anna wants to know who must answer, and Leo asks who needs to answer; implied only those subject to source tax.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Initial statement: all non-Swiss employees (anyone without a Swiss passport) are subject to source tax.

anchors.quote: All the non-Swiss employees. Simple as that. If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: The Zurich source tax calculator (canton website, yields the tariff code) is used for every employee regardless of where they actually belong; Anna acknowledges this is not exactly correct but it is what they do for now, and Leo agrees to keep it.

anchors.quote: I use the Zurich calculator on the canton's website. The one that gives you the tariff code.
For everybody I use Zurich, by the way. I know it's not exactly how it works, but that's what we do for now.
Understood. We'll keep that for now.

subject: source_tax_calculator
statement: Today HR clicks through the Zurich calculator manually using the employee's answers.

anchors.quote: I sit with the answers and click through it.

subject: address
statement: HR needs the employee's full postal address.

anchors.quote: Yes, I need the address, obviously. The full address.

subject: address
statement: The address must be complete with street, house number, postcode, town and country, because HR posts many documents to employees.

anchors.quote: Street, number, postcode, town, country. We post a lot of documents to people, so it has to be complete.

subject: address
statement: Nothing beyond a normal postal address (as written on an envelope) is needed for the address.

anchors.quote: No, no. Just a normal address, the way you would write it on an envelope.

subject: photo
statement: Anna would like the form to ask for a photo for employee badges, since phone photos taken at reception are poor.

anchors.quote: Oh, that would be so nice, actually. For the badges.
Could the form ask for a photo?

subject: photo
statement: No photo is collected for now; security is changing the badge system next year and the topic is postponed to next year.

anchors.quote: Let's not do that now. Forget the photo for the moment, we'll talk about it next year.

subject: pension_fund
statement: Muster AG's pension fund is Pensionskasse Muster, which has an old portal; Anna will send screenshots of it.

anchors.quote: We're with Pensionskasse Muster. They have a portal, it's quite old. I'll send you some screenshots of it after this call

subject: first_working_day
statement: The employee's first working day is needed (for the pension fund) and is the most important item; the employee should confirm it.

anchors.quote: I need their first working day. That's the number one thing, and I ask them to confirm it

judge_note: First working day and confirmation are supported, but 'for the pension fund' is only implied by Leo's question and 'most important item' is 'number one thing' for the fund context.

subject: first_working_day
statement: The first working day changes often, e.g. when people negotiate an earlier exit with their old employer; a missed update (Julia) caused a wrong date at the fund and weeks of fixing.

anchors.quote: because it moves more often than you'd think.
She moved her first working day to the 15th of March, and I didn't update it.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Pension fund insurance starts on the first day of the month following the first working day (e.g. first working day 15 March -> insurance start 1 April).

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month. So for her that was the first of April

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Exception: if the first working day is exactly the first of a month, insurance starts on that same day.

anchors.quote: Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Consolidated: insurance_start_date is derived from first_working_day: if first_working_day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise it starts on the 1st of the following month. It should be derived, not asked.

anchors.quote: because insurance starts on the first of the following month.
Unless somebody starts exactly on the first, of course, then it's just that day.

judge_note: Reasonable inference combining the rule and exception; 'derive not ask' is a sensible design reading.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund asks for the employee's civil status.

anchors.quote: Yes, the civil status. They ask for that.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: If the employee is married, the pension fund wants the spouse's date of birth.

anchors.quote: And if someone is married, they want the date of birth of the husband or wife.

subject: civil_status
statement: Civil status options are, per Anna's uncertain recollection, single, married, divorced, and 'I think' widowed; she defers to the pension fund screenshots for the actual list.

anchors.quote: I'd have to look. You'll see it in the screenshots. Single, married, divorced, I think widowed.

subject: civil_status
statement: At least one current employee (Daniel in finance) is in a registered partnership, so this civil status occurs in practice.

anchors.quote: we do have one colleague in a registered partnership. Daniel, in finance.

subject: civil_status
statement: Unknown how the pension fund's screen handles registered partnership and whether the fund wants the partner's details (e.g. date of birth) in that case.

anchors.quote: I honestly don't know what the fund's screen does in that case, or if they want the partner's details too.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Correction: non-Swiss employees holding a C permit are not subject to source tax; they are treated like Swiss people for this.

anchors.quote: So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.
Okay, so non-Swiss, but not with a C permit.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Example: Maria in sales is Portuguese with a C permit and does not pay source tax.

anchors.quote: I'm thinking of Maria in sales, she's Portuguese, and she doesn't do source tax at all. She has a C permit.

subject: timing_data
statement: Anna offered to get numbers from the payroll person on how long the source tax process takes.

anchors.quote: Do you want some numbers on how long this takes? I could get that for you from our payroll person.

judge_note: 'This' in context refers to the source tax topic; reasonable.

subject: it_equipment
statement: Laptops/IT equipment are out of scope; IT has its own process.

anchors.quote: IT does laptops, they have their own process, keep them out of this, please.

subject: permit_reminder
statement: Anna would love the form to remind employees to bring their permit (on the first day), because half of them forget; wording to be looked at later, not decided.

anchors.quote: What I would love is if the form could remind people to bring their permit. Half of them forget.
We can look at the wording later.

subject: spouse_employment
statement: For married employees subject to source tax, the Zurich calculator asks whether the spouse works.

anchors.quote: It changes the questions in the calculator, yes. Whether the husband or wife works.

judge_note: Calculator asking whether the spouse works is supported, but 'Zurich' is not mentioned in these units.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: An employee married to a Swiss national or to a C permit holder who lives in Switzerland is not subject to source tax (e.g. Tomás: Brazilian, B permit, Swiss wife, living in Winterthur).

anchors.quote: If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Brazilian, B permit, but his wife is Swiss, and they live in Winterthur. So no source tax for him.

subject: spouse_data
statement: Today HR checks the spouse exemption by hand and asks for spouse data by email, which takes very long.

anchors.quote: I always have to check that one by hand.
I ask them by email, and it takes forever.

judge_note: Anna says she checks by hand and asks by email, which takes forever.

subject: spouse_nationality
statement: For married employees (source tax determination), the spouse's nationality is needed.

anchors.quote: So you need to know about the spouse as well.
Yes. Their nationality, their permit if they have one, and that they live here.

subject: spouse_permit_type
statement: For married employees (source tax determination), the spouse's permit type is needed if the spouse has one.

anchors.quote: their permit if they have one

subject: spouse_permit_type
statement: The spouse's permit is only relevant when the spouse is not Swiss (Swiss nationals have no permit).

anchors.quote: their permit if they have one

judge_note: Reasonable reading: 'if they have one' implies permit only applies to those who have one, i.e. non-Swiss; slight inference.

subject: spouse_residence_country
statement: For married employees (source tax determination), whether the spouse lives in Switzerland is needed.
judge_note: 'That they live here' means Switzerland, reasonable.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Employees who live abroad and work in Switzerland are always subject to source tax, regardless of nationality (e.g. Stefan, Swiss, lives in Konstanz; a warehouse employee lives in Liechtenstein).

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here. And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way.
Stefan is actually Swiss, and he still has it.
So someone living abroad and working here always does it?

subject: cross_border
statement: Muster AG has a few employees living across the border (Germany, Liechtenstein).

anchors.quote: We have a few who live across the border. Stefan lives in Konstanz, and there's a woman in the warehouse who lives in Liechtenstein.

subject: cross_border
statement: For employees living abroad the calculator asks more questions (Germany has its own forms); Anna cannot name them, and Leo defers to the calculator for the details.

anchors.quote: And with them the calculator gets much more complicated, there are more questions. Germany has its own forms, I can never remember what they're called.
Okay, that's fine, the calculator will tell us.

subject: subject_to_source_tax
statement: Consolidated final rule (Anna hedged completeness with 'I think'): an employee is subject to source tax if residence_country is not CH (regardless of nationality). If living in CH: not subject if nationality is CH; not subject if permit_type is C; not subject if married to a spouse who is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in CH; otherwise subject.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.
So, not the people with a C permit. They're treated like Swiss people for this.
If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here. And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way.

judge_note: Reasonable consolidation of the stated rules; the C-permit equivalence to Swiss and exemptions are all stated.

subject: nationality
statement: The employee's nationality is needed to determine source tax liability.

anchors.quote: If you don't have a Swiss passport, you do source tax.

subject: permit_type
statement: Non-Swiss employees' permit type (at least whether it is a C permit) is needed to determine source tax liability.

anchors.quote: So, not the people with a C permit.

subject: residence_country
statement: The employee's country of residence is needed to determine source tax liability (living abroad means always subject).

anchors.quote: Those people do source tax because they work here and they don't live here.

subject: spouse_data
statement: Spouse nationality, permit and residence only need to be asked when the employee is married and the spouse exemption could apply (i.e. employee is non-Swiss without C permit and lives in CH).

anchors.quote: If you're married to someone Swiss, or to someone with a C permit, and that person lives here, then you don't do source tax either.
And there it doesn't matter what passport you have, by the way.

judge_note: Gist is reasonable, but the explicit condition about when to ask spouse data is not stated; it is an inferred design choice.

subject: spouse_residence_country
statement: 'Lives here' in Anna's statements means living in Switzerland.

anchors.quote: they work here and they don't live here.

judge_note: Context (Winterthur, 'live here' vs living abroad) supports Switzerland.

subject: project_timing
statement: Anna asked when the product will be available; Leo will reply this week after reviewing the screenshots.

anchors.quote: Only the timing. When can we have this?
I'll come back to you on that this week, once we've gone through your screenshots.

subject: last_name
statement: The pension fund registration form has a required 'Last name' text field.

subject: date_of_birth

statement: The Canton dropdown offers exactly 26 Swiss cantons: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. There is no option for living outside Switzerland.
judge_note: All 26 options listed in order (E16-E41); absence of an outside-Switzerland option follows from the list.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: The pension fund registration form has a required 'Insurance start date' field in the 'Insurance' section.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: Insurance start date is entered as DD.MM.YYYY and must be the 1st of a month.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

subject: civil_status
statement: The pension fund registration form has a required 'Civil status' dropdown.

subject: civil_status
statement: The Civil status dropdown offers exactly four options: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: The pension fund registration form has a 'Spouse's date of birth' field, marked required when shown.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: Spouse's date of birth is entered in the format DD.MM.YYYY.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: 'Spouse's date of birth' appears only when Civil status is 'Married': it is shown in screenshots 05 and 07 (civil status Married) and absent in screenshot 04 (civil status Single) and in 01, 02, 03, 06 (civil status not selected).
judge_note: Shown for Married (05, 07) and absent for Single (04), and no spouse field appears in 01/03 units, but screenshot 06 and 02 are not evidenced and 'only when' is an inference.

subject: required_fields_validation
statement: Submitting the form with missing required fields shows the banner 'Please correct the highlighted fields.' and highlights each empty required field.
judge_note: The banner text is shown in screenshot 06, but the units don't show the submit trigger or that every empty required field is highlighted (only an error-highlighted spouse field in 07).

subject: required_fields_validation
statement: Each missing required field shows an error of the form '<Field label> is required.': 'First name is required.', 'Last name is required.', 'Date of birth is required.', 'Canton is required.', 'Insurance start date is required.', 'Civil status is required.'
judge_note: All six error messages appear verbatim in the units with the stated pattern.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: When Civil status is Married and Spouse's date of birth is empty, registration is rejected with 'Spouse's date of birth is required.'

anchors.quote: Spouse's date of birth is required.

judge_note: Civil status Married with Spouse's date of birth required error shown; the field value is not visible but the error implies empty, reasonable.

subject: pension_portal
statement: The form is the 'Register new employee' page of the Pensionskasse Muster employer portal, used by the employer Muster AG under 'Insured persons'.
judge_note: Title, breadcrumb, portal name, employer Muster AG and Insured persons breadcrumb all shown.

subject: residence_canton
statement: The Canton dropdown lists only Swiss cantons; it is unclear what to enter for an employee living abroad (e.g. cross-border commuter), and whether 'Canton' means residence canton or work canton.
judge_note: Only Zug and Zurich options are visible, so 'only Swiss cantons' is plausible but the ambiguity about residence/work canton is the extractor's inference, not in the units.

subject: civil_status
statement: The Civil status list has no option for registered partnership, separated, or other statuses; it is open how employees with such statuses are registered and whether a partner's date of birth is then needed.
judge_note: List shows only Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed; the open questions are a reasonable inferred reading.

subject: spouse_date_of_birth
statement: No screenshot shows the form with Civil status 'Divorced' or 'Widowed'; whether Spouse's date of birth is hidden for those values is assumed but not proven.
judge_note: Units show the Divorced/Widowed options exist; absence of screenshots for them is not contradicted, and the open-question reading is reasonable.

subject: insurance_start_date
statement: The portal requires an insurance start date on the 1st of a month but does not say how it relates to the first working day (e.g. 1st of the start month or next month); the derivation rule insurance_start_date is open.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

judge_note: Hint says must be the 1st of a month and nothing relates it to first working day; reasonable open item.

subject: date_validation
statement: No screenshot shows the error for an invalid date format or an insurance start date that is not the 1st of a month; the wording and any other date constraints (e.g. past/future limits) are unknown.

anchors.quote: DD.MM.YYYY. Must be the 1st of a month.

judge_note: Only the required error is shown for the insurance start date in these units; other error wording is unknown, a reasonable inferred open point.
